summary: Coca-Cola is a highly profitable consumer-defensive beverage company (gross margin 61.7%, operating margin 35.1%, net margin 27.8%, ROE 43.4%) generating robust operating cash flow of $14.63B TTM. However, the stock looks fully valued: trailing P/E 25.44, forward P/E 23.23, P/B 10.35 and a steep PEG of 4.23, with only ~6.3% upside to the $85.97 mean analyst target from $80.91. The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage (Debt/Equity 124.94; $44.65B debt vs $13.82B cash), and while the latest quarter grew strongly (revenue +12.1%, earnings +18.2% YoY), the annual revenue trend has decelerated to roughly +1.7% in 2025. Sentiment is constructive — low beta (0.35), +16.2% over 52 weeks near the high, and a 'buy' consensus from 24 analysts. Direct competitive/moat metrics are absent, limiting a complete assessment.

dimensions.rationale: The latest quarter showed strong year-over-year growth of 12.1% in revenue (E11) and 18.2% in earnings (E12). However, the annual revenue trend is decelerating: $43.0B (2022) → $45.8B (2023, +6.5%) → $47.1B (2024, +2.8%) → $47.9B (2025, +1.7%) (E28). The strong recent quarter supports a positive rating, but the marked annual deceleration tempers confidence.

Margins are exceptional and consistent across the P&L: gross margin 61.7% (E13), operating margin 35.1% (E14), and net profit margin 27.8% (E15). Return on equity is very high at 43.4% (E16). Multiple direct, current data points agree on best-in-class profitability.

Leverage is elevated: Debt/Equity is 124.94 (E21) with total debt of $44.65B against total cash of $13.82B (E20, E19), implying net debt of roughly $30.8B. Liquidity is adequate with a current ratio of 1.36 (E22). The high leverage is offset by a substantial cash position and acceptable short-term liquidity, leaving the picture genuinely balanced.

Multiples are full for a slow-growing staple: trailing P/E 25.44 (E7), forward P/E 23.23 (E8), Price/Book 10.35 (E9), and a notably high PEG of 4.23 (E10). At $80.91 (E2) the stock sits only ~6.3% below the $85.97 mean analyst target (E3), implying limited upside. The elevated PEG in particular signals the price is rich relative to growth.

Operating cash flow is strong at $14.63B TTM (E18), but free cash flow is far lower at $3.12B TTM (E17), implying a large gap (~$11.5B) between the two. Robust operating cash generation is a positive, but the low FCF conversion is a meaningful offset, leaving the dimension balanced. The evidence does not break out capital expenditures to explain the divergence.

No direct competitive evidence is provided — there are no market-share figures, brand-value metrics, pricing-power data, or competitor comparisons. Only a sector label (Consumer Defensive / Beverages, E1) and a qualitative business description listing brands (E29) are available, which are insufficient to judge the durability of any moat. Per the discipline of this tool, this is marked as a data gap rather than assumed.

Price momentum is favorable: the stock is up 16.2% over 52 weeks (E25) and trades at $80.91 (E2), near its 52-week high of $84.04 (E4) and well above its low of $65.35 (E5). Analyst sentiment is constructive with a 'buy' consensus from 24 analysts (E26, E27) and a mean target of $85.97 (E3), while a beta of 0.35 (E24) indicates low volatility. Multiple agreeing signals support a positive read.

Several concrete risk signals are present: a stretched valuation (PEG 4.23, P/E 25.44, P/B 10.35 — E10, E7, E9), elevated leverage (Debt/Equity 124.94, $44.65B debt — E21, E20), free cash flow of only $3.12B versus $14.63B operating cash flow (E17, E18), and decelerating annual revenue growth toward +1.7% (E28). The recent news headlines (E30–E34) are vague or off-topic and were not treated as risk evidence.
